Thus z_j=(3/8) times the sum of the first j powers of 1/16. Since |1/16|<1, these positions approach (3/8)/(1-1/16)=2/5. The alternating turnaround positions approach 3/2+(2/5)/4=8/5. Put x=AC>0. The internal angle-bisector theorem gives BD/3=10/x, so BC=3+30/x. Clearing denominators in the three strict triangle inequalities gives (x+10)(x-3)>0, x^2-7x+30>0, and (x-15)(x+2)<0. The middle quadratic is always positive because its leading coefficient is positive and its discriminant is -71. Hence exactly 3<x<15 is feasible. Conversely, these side lengths form a triangle whose angle bisector has CD=3. Thus m+n=3+15=18.

Model acquaintances as the cycle edges together with five opposite-pair edges, and count perfect matchings. With no opposite pair there are two alternating cycle matchings. With at least one opposite pair selected, every remaining path along the circle must have an even number of vertices; equivalently, consecutive selected endpoints have odd cyclic gaps. This permits 1,3, or 5 opposite pairs, not 2 or 4. There are respectively 5,5,1 valid selections, each with a unique completion by adjacent pairs. The total is 2+5+5+1=13. People are distinct; rotations are not identified.

Let ABC have side s and altitude h. The outer triangle partitions into ABC and three triangles, each with a base of length 4s along an extended original side and perpendicular height 3h. Each added triangle therefore has 12 times the area of ABC, giving a total ratio 1+3*12=37. Alternatively, the cosine law with lengths 3s and 4s and included angle 120 degrees gives each outer side squared as 37s^2; the outer triangle is equilateral, so its area ratio is 37.

Let the leftmost coordinate be k>0. The logarithm graph is strictly concave, so the simple quadrilateral follows the four points in increasing x-order and closes along the endpoint chord. Shoelace, or subtracting the large endpoint trapezoid from the three unit-width trapezoids, gives area ln(k+1)+ln(k+2)-ln(k)-ln(k+3)=ln[1+2/(k(k+3))]. Equating this to ln(91/90) yields k(k+3)=180. The roots are 12 and -15, so positivity gives k=12.
